concerns.text: T015 (Motion filtering) is listed as a dependency for T017, but T015 is marked as unchecked/missing implementation while T017 is marked as 'Depends on T015'. Furthermore, T012 (Data Ingestion) is marked 'FAILED: unspecified', yet T015 and T017 depend on its output (raw data). This creates a broken dependency chain where consumer tasks (T017) are scheduled before their producer (T012) is complete or even defined.

T023 (Aggregation logic) is marked as missing/rejected, yet T024a (Phase-shuffled null model) and T026 (Save metrics) explicitly depend on T023. T024a cannot validate the metric if the metric (Variability_Metric) has not been collapsed/aggregated by T023. This violates the 'Producer before Consumer' rule for the core data artifact.

T036 (Merge results) depends on T034 (regression_summary.json), but T034 is marked as missing/rejected. Additionally, T036 depends on T026 (metrics.csv), which in turn depends on the missing T023. The entire US3 output chain is blocked by missing upstream producers (T023, T034).

T015a (Calculate success rate) depends on T036 (final_results.csv) and T015/T017 (exclusion_log.csv). Since T015, T017, and T036 are all blocked by missing upstream tasks (T012, T023, T034), T015a has no valid execution path. The dependency graph is circular or broken at the root.

T039b (Profile memory) and T039c (Run benchmark) depend on T039a (Batch processing implementation), which is marked as missing. Furthermore, T039b requires the full pipeline to run (implied by 'benchmark script'), but the pipeline is broken due to missing US1/US2/US3 implementations (T012, T023, T034). The benchmark tasks are scheduled before the system they are meant to test exists.

T005 is marked '[Depends on T004]', but T004 is marked as completed (checked). However, T005 is also marked as completed (checked) despite T015 (which depends on T005's logic) being missing. The status flags (checked/unchecked) are inconsistent with the dependency annotations, creating confusion about which foundational tasks are actually ready.
